t:
(a) Section 2108(3) of title 5, United States Code, is amended by inserting “or the General Accounting Office” after “the Senior Executive Service”. 
    (b) Subsection 5102(a)(1) of such title is amended by striking out “or” at the end of clause (vii), by inserting “or” at the end of clause (viii), and by adding at the end thereof the following:

“(ix) the General Accounting Office;”. 
    (c)
        (1) Paragraph (1) of section 5108(c) of such title is repealed.  
        (2) 
Paragraphs (2), (3), and (4) of such section are redesignated paragraphs (1), (2), and (3), respectively.  
    (d) Section 5342(a)(1) of such title is amended by striking out “or” at the end of subparagraph (H), by inserting “or” at the end of subparagraph (I), and by adding at the end thereof the following:


“(J) 
the General Accounting Office;”.
 
    (e)
        (1) Subchapter III of chapter 73 of title 5, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end thereof the following new section:


“§ 7328. General Accounting Office employees
“The preceding provisions of this subchapter shall not apply to employees of the General Accounting Office.”.
 
        (2) 
The chapter analysis for chapter 73 of title 5, United States Code, is amended by adding after the item relating to section 7327 the following new item:


“7328. General Accounting Office employees.”.


 
        (3) 
Subsections (a), (b), and (d) of section 311 of the Budget and Accounting Act, 1921 (31 U.S.C. 52) are amended to read as follows:

“(a) The Comptroller General shall appoint, fix the pay of, and remove employees of the General Accounting Office under the General Accounting Office Personnel Act of 1980. 
“(b) All officers and employees of the General Accounting Office shall perform such duties as may be assigned to them by the Comptroller General.”.

 
        (4) 
Subsections (e) and (f) of such section are redesignated subsections (c) and (d), respectively.
  
    (f) Section 13 of the Federal Employees Pay Act of 1946 (31 U.S.C. 46a) is repealed. 
    (g) Section 717(a) of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (42 U.S.C. 2000e–16) is amended by striking out “(other than the General Accounting Office)”.

fable.w: The section consists of technical and conforming amendments to federal personnel statutes governing General Accounting Office employees, all of whom are inside the federal government. The tempting reading is that striking the GAO exclusion from section 717(a) of the Civil Rights Act creates a right to sue, but the text merely adjusts statutory coverage for federal employees. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or consultation with any outside party before a federal decision.
fable.s: The Comptroller General shall appoint, fix the pay of, and remove employees of the General Accounting Office under the General Accounting Office Personnel Act of 1980.

opus.w: This section only makes technical changes to federal personnel law for the General Accounting Office (GAO): job classification, pay, how other subchapter rules apply, and the Comptroller General's power to hire and fire. Everyone affected is a federal official or employee, and no outside party is consulted or given a role in any federal decision. The tempting reading treats the Civil Rights Act amendment as a right to sue, but it only changes coverage for the government's own employees. It creates no outside public participation in a federal decision.
opus.s: The Comptroller General shall appoint, fix the pay of, and remove employees of the General Accounting Office under the General Accounting Office Personnel Act of 1980.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** subsection (g) brings GAO employees under section 717 of the Civil Rights Act, which deals with discrimination claims. That might look like giving someone a right to challenge a government decision. It isn't. The section is a set of technical changes to the personnel rules for GAO employees, and those employees are federal staff, so they are inside the government. Nothing here asks the government to consult outsiders before deciding something: there are no hearings, comment periods, rulemaking requirements, advisory bodies, or consultation with states or the public.

qwen_chat.w: This section deals with the internal personnel management of the General Accounting Office (GAO), a federal agency. The definition states that federal agencies and their employees are inside the federal government. Therefore, rules regarding the appointment, pay, and removal of GAO employees are intra-governmental matters and do not involve consultation or coordination with parties outside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: (a) The Comptroller General shall appoint, fix the pay of, and remove employees of the General Accounting Office under the General Accounting Office Personnel Act of 1980.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the General Accounting Office (GAO) is an independent agency, its employees are "outside" the executive branch, and thus internal personnel rules involving them constitute participation. However, the definition explicitly states that "federal agencies, federal officials, and federal employees are all INSIDE the federal government." The GAO is a federal agency, and its employees are federal employees. Therefore, any interaction or rule-making concerning them is intra-governmental.
